key_insight: OmniPlan turns free-form planning intents into a unified preference vector and uses adaptive expert selection to balance fast execution with near-optimal network planning decisions.
engineering_relevance: This framework is useful for real-world infrastructure planning where operators need low-latency decisions that still respect multiple competing objectives and changing user preferences.
method: LLM interpreter maps natural-language intents to a quantifiable user-preference vector
Mixture-of-experts combines MIP solvers, heuristics, and DRL planners
DRL-based expert configuration tunes objective weights for user-specific trade-offs
evidence_signal: In a real-world distributed ML offloading testbed, OmniPlan achieved near-optimal, low-execution-time planning, cutting latency by up to 97.8% and device resource consumption by up to 11.5%.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable intent interpretation and expert selection; misread user preferences or poor weight tuning could reduce optimality or robustness.
paper_title: OmniPlan: An Adaptive Framework for Timely and Near-Optimal Network Planning Optimization
